AfterObtained.maps_to: after_obtained (sts2_rl/relics/cauldron.py:27-40) -- five PotionRewards, each offered through RunState.offer_potion
AfterObtained.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the relic's whole effect is ported. sts2_rl/relics/cauldron.py:27-40 offers DynamicVars['Potions'] == 5 PotionRewards on pickup through RunState.offer_potion, each rolled by generate_random_potion on run.player_rng.rewards. WAS: a behaviourless stub.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the stub's premise -- 'out-of-combat pickup effect, stub' -- is false; the sim dispatches after_obtained and has a full potion pipeline
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the stub is gone. sts2_rl/relics/cauldron.py:27-40 implements after_obtained -- five independent potions, each populated by its own `generate_random_potion(run.player_rng.rewards)` (CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat off PlayerRng.Rewards, two draws apiece, with a per-reward blacklist so ids may repeat) and each offered through `run.offer_potion` -- which is Cauldron.cs:31-55's shipping arm. WAS: the port declared only id/name/rarity/pickup-flag and the player got nothing.

guards.what: G2: the TestMode arm (Cauldron.cs:16-23, 40-46) is not the shipping behaviour
guards.rationale: Recorded because the sibling relic in this very batch, relic/calling_bell, ported the TestMode arm of the identical OfferCustom pattern by mistake (its guard G1). Cauldron's test arm hands out FlexPotion/WeakPotion/VulnerablePotion/StrengthPotion/DexterityPotion in order; the shipping arm at :48-52 is five unpopulated PotionRewards, each of which rolls from the potion pool. `TestMode.TurnOnInternal` (TestMode.cs:38) has no caller under src/, so the shipping arm is what a fix must implement. Verdict faithful because the port implements neither arm -- there is nothing here to be wrong about beyond G1.
